Plot posterior model probabilities

Source: R/plot-models.R
plot_models.Rd

Display the posterior probabilities of the individual models in a fitted model-averaged meta-analysis. Each column is one full model and its width is its posterior probability. Rows describe the model's fitted components.

Usage

plot_models(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RoBMA'
plot_models(
  x,
  parameter = NULL,
  component = "auto",
  factor_view = "levels",
  mixture_view = "inclusion",
  group_labels = FALSE,
  labels = NULL,
  decreasing = TRUE,
  col = NULL,
  col_bias = NULL,
  legend = FALSE,
  legend_position = "bottom",
  plot_type = "base",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a fitted model-averaged object, such as a fit from RoBMA() or BMA().

...

additional arguments for methods.

parameter

an ordered character vector of model component, term, or factor-level selectors. Use NULL to show the model components, including random-effect rows, followed by the location and scale terms. Random-effect inclusion rows use the labels printed by summary.brma() and appear before publication bias. Use qualified selectors such as "mu_year", "log_tau_year", or "mu_delivery[online]" to disambiguate terms or levels.

component

component to select from: "auto", "mods" (also "location"), "scale", "bias", or "random".

factor_view

"levels" shows a row per fitted factor level and "terms" shows one neutral inclusion row per factor term. Supply a single setting or named overrides for individual terms. Unspecified terms use "levels".

mixture_view

"inclusion" displays each member's declared null or alternative status. "model" shows one categorical row for the mixture. "individual" shows one row for each declared member, including null members. Supply a single setting or named overrides for individual terms. Unspecified terms use "inclusion".

group_labels

whether to display group headings beside the rows.

labels

named character vector of row label overrides. Use stable selectors such as "mu", "mu_year", "mu_delivery[online]", or "bias[PET]" (when the mixture member is named PET). Overrides also update the mixture labels in the legend.

decreasing

whether to draw models in decreasing posterior probability order.

col

named colors for positive, negative, included, and excluded. Defaults are blue, red, black, and white, respectively.

col_bias

named colors for bias and no_bias or for publication-bias mixture members, using their names from summary_models() or qualified member selectors of the form "bias[PET]". Member-specific colors override bias and no-bias colors in categorical and individual views. Use qualified selectors for members named bias or no_bias. This argument requires a displayed publication-bias component.

legend

whether to show the color legend.

legend_position

location of the legend, "bottom" or "top".

plot_type

"base" for base graphics or "ggplot" for ggplot2.

Value

Invisibly NULL for base graphics or a ggplot object for ggplot2. The ggplot object has an integer n_rows attribute giving the number of displayed rows after selection and expansion, excluding the group headings and legend.

Details

The column widths come from the same joint indicator draws as summary_models(x, type = "individual"). Choosing rows changes the displayed information while keeping the fitted models and their widths. Ungated coefficients can appear alongside the model components. Select the main components by "mu", "tau", "bias", and "rho" for an available heterogeneity allocation mixture. Use qualified selectors for moderators with those names.

Inclusion uses the null or alternative assignment of the active prior member, or the fitted inclusion gate. In the inclusion view, directional colors indicate the sign of the posterior median within that full model on the fitted predictor scale. If the predictors were centered or standardized during fitting, intercept and moderator directions refer to that parameterization. Heterogeneity, heterogeneity allocation, publication bias, random-effect gates, whole factors, and coefficients with a median of zero use neutral inclusion colors. Factor level rows share the factor's inclusion gate. Treatment contrasts show coefficients relative to the reference level and omit the reference row. Mean-difference and orthonormal contrasts show deviations from the equally weighted mean of the factor levels.

See also

summary_models(), plot.brma()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- RoBMA(yi = d, sei = se, data = Bem2011, measure = "SMD", seed = 1)
p <- plot_models(fit, parameter = c("mu", "bias"),
                 mixture_view = c(bias = "individual"), plot_type = "ggplot")
attr(p, "n_rows")
p
} # }
